exposure: Duration of pushing (more than 1 hour vs. less than 1 hour)
Mode of delivery (spontaneous vaginal delivery vs. operative delivery)
Longer duration of active pushing during labor
cohort: 197 nulliparous women with neuraxial analgesia and complete cervical dilatation
finding: The study found that a wider angle of progression at rest and a larger change in angle of progression during pushing were the best predictors of spontaneous vaginal delivery and shorter pushing duration in nulliparous women.
mod_finding: Spontaneous vaginal delivery was significantly more common in women with a nonocciput posterior fetal position, a wider angle of progression, a shorter head-perineum distance and head-symphysis distance, and a lower fetal head station.
